failure_conditions.condition: The output has an evidenced intended purpose or downstream task for which factual accuracy, evidentiary fidelity, technical correctness, source integrity, traceability, uncertainty handling or equivalent epistemic assurance is materially consequential; identify the requirement for the actual workflow stage, including any drafting function.

failure_conditions.condition: The artefact is supplied, represented, propagated, incorporated, submitted or accepted as usable for the reliance-bearing purpose or workflow stage without its required accuracy or epistemic threshold being satisfied. success_conditions.condition: An epistemic artefact is proposed for reliance with material error consequences.

Content accuracy and assurance meet the requirement for the actual purpose and workflow stage. Specificity, certainty and framing remain proportionate to source quality, independence, traceability, uncertainty and temporal fitness, without distorting material meaning.
success_conditions.assessment: No affirmative patient-specific assurance pathway established.

success_conditions.condition: The output, supporting evidence and reliance decision demonstrate fitness for that bounded use and show that lower-assurance material remained restricted from unsupported higher reliance. A provisional label or an expectation of human review alone is insufficient.
success_conditions.assessment: Nominal clinical review and litigation survival do not prove a protected reliance decision.

exclusion_comparison: Empirical care prediction is not fiction. Approximation may fit estimation, but cannot automatically excuse use as a binding coverage rule; alleged promotion remains disputed. No simple verification omission, stale-check or provenance-only issue suffices.
amendment_delta: Explicit operational reliance applies to the trace-linked decisions above; no bad-outcome-to-belief inference. Hindsight-only mistake does not prove insufficient assurance; known boundary crossing without separate assurance defect excluded. Success requires responsive bounded use, not mere recognition.

before_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Plaintiffs allege that nH Predict’s expected care-duration output became a practically determinative individual coverage cutoff despite contrary clinical information. That is the class-defined evidence-to-authority mechanism if established, but the court still treats the model’s dispositive role as a merits question. Coverage documents represented clinical services staff and physicians as the decision route, while plaintiffs allege nH Predict was used instead. The alleged displacement matches required governance routing, but remains medium-confidence because the factual substitution has not been adjudicated.
